correctness.rationale: Identify each rook cell with root edge of K_(m,n). Undominated rook vertices correspond precisely to root edges between unused roots plus selected isolated matching edges. For root-edge set H, potential Phi=number used roots minus number isolated selected edges gains 1 or 2 per legal addition; first nonmatching step gains 2. Thus any sequence with nontrivial component has length<=m+n-1. To attain equality, exactly one step has gain 2, no isolated selected edge survives, and the last unused root must enter at that gain-2 step. This forces a matching covering all but one root, possible iff |m-n|=1; successive attachments are forced structurally. The matching/attachment choices count product (a+1)! a! times a (a-1)! times product_(j=1)^(a-1)(2j+1). An explicit row/column sequence constructs length m+n-2 otherwise. Independent full open-neighborhood dynamic programming agrees on 2x3: 72, 3x4:12960, and multiple other boards.
residual_risks: Independent finite verification corroborates but cannot establish the all-parameter proof.
